newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares up in moderate post-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares up in moderate post-holiday trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares rose on Monday as trade resumed after a five-day holiday with local investor demand focused on high performing stock, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.30 percent to 153.26 points in moderate turnover of 428,042 dinars ($604,579).
Trade was dominated by activity on select blue-chip, including Jordan Cement Factories which rose 0.11 dinars to 3.76 dinars in trade worth 27,130 dinars.

Brokers said the firm, which has been steadily rising on prospects of better earnings after the government recently raised retail prices of locally sold cement, suffered from a shortage of readily available stock on offer.
Healthy activity in the parallel market which lists newly established on NAMICO which manufactures engineering products helped to cushion the overall market.

NAMICO rose 0.03 dinars to 0.65 dinars in 23,693 dinars worth of trade. But heaviest traded was Arab Financial Investment which rose 0.02 dinars to 0.49 dinars in trade worth 57,085 dinars with 116,500 shares exchanging hands.
But trade was generally quiet in the first day of business after a five-day break, a public holiday to mark the Moslem Eid al Adha feast.

The exchange also continued a pattern of bargian hunting activity by mostly local investors in a handful of speculative and undervalued blue-chip stock prompted by recent falls which have made current price levels attractive, brokers said.

Recent political uncertainty over the fate of Middle East peace combined with a lack of liquidity has recently depressed sentiment and prompted outside buyers and institutional investors to remain on the sidelines.

Jordan Phosphate Mines rose 0.05 dinars in a large bloc sale worth 160,000 dinars which nearly accounted for half the day's volume. Market heavyweight Arab Bank was unchanged at 256.00 dinars in the second largest trading volume worth 128,020 dinars.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.37 dinars to 81.20 points, 2.63 percent down from the start of the year.
